findings.title: Imported feed/article HTML is rendered without sanitization
findings.body: This creates posts with the `raw_html` cook method, for which `Post#cook` returns the supplied HTML unchanged. `PollFeed` supplies external feed content directly to this method, and the embed view emits `raw post.cooked`, so a feed item containing `<script>`, event-handler attributes, or dangerous URLs executes as the Discourse origin for anyone viewing the imported topic/embed. Feed content must be sanitized with a strict HTML allowlist (and the generated source link escaped) before it is stored or rendered.

findings.title: The host allowlist is bypassed after an HTTP redirect
findings.body: `TopicRetriever` checks only the hostname of the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects and this method does not validate the redirect destination. An attacker who can use an open redirect on the configured embeddable host can make the Discourse server request arbitrary HTTP endpoints, including internal services or cloud metadata addresses; the fetched response may then be imported into a public topic. Disable redirects or validate every redirect target, including resolved IP addresses, against the allowed destination policy.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can flood the retrieval job queue
findings.body: The only access check is the `Referer` header, which arbitrary HTTP clients can forge, and this action enqueues a job before the worker validates the URL or applies its per-URL throttle. A caller can send many GET requests with a forged allowed Referer and distinct `embed_url` values to create unbounded Sidekiq work (and, for allowed-host URLs, outbound fetches). Validate the target before enqueueing and add a server-side rate limit or signed integration token; Referer alone is not an authentication boundary.

findings.title: The outer transaction lets post-processing jobs run before the imported post commits
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues post-processing work after its own `Post.transaction`, but that nested transaction joins this surrounding `Topic.transaction`. Consequently `PostCreator` enqueues jobs while this outer transaction is still open, so a separate Sidekiq connection can run before it can see the post. If `TopicEmbed.create!` subsequently fails (for example, due to the unique URL index during a concurrent import), the outer transaction rolls the post back after jobs and MessageBus events have already been emitted for it. Defer those side effects with an after-commit hook or restructure the creation so the post and embed commit before jobs are enqueued.

findings.title: Feed polling uses String#scrub on Ruby versions supported by the application
findings.body: `String#scrub` was introduced in Ruby 2.1, while this application retains MRI 1.9 support (the Gemfile has an `mri_19` dependency path). On those supported deployments every feed item reaches this line and raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the polling run; since the job disables Sidekiq retries, later items are skipped. Use a Ruby-version-compatible encoding cleanup. This expression also needs to handle feeds without a `content` field, since `i.content` may be nil for otherwise valid RSS/Atom entries.

findings.title: Direct embed retrieval does not load open-uri
findings.body: This method calls `open` with an HTTP URL but does not require `open-uri`, which is what extends `Kernel#open` to handle URLs. The only new `require 'open-uri'` is in the unrelated `PollFeed` job. With feed polling disabled (the default), `retrieve_topic` reaches this method without loading `PollFeed`, so normal `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local filename and raises instead of retrieving the article. Require `open-uri` in this model or in the retrieval component that uses it.

findings.title: A failed worker can leave an embed URL throttled forever
findings.body: The throttle lease is established with `SETNX` and its expiry is applied in a separate Redis command. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` succeeds, the key has no TTL. Every later non-staff retrieval for that URL sees the key and returns without importing it, leaving the embed on its loading page indefinitely. Set the value and expiration atomically (for example, Redis `SET ... NX EX 60` or a Lua script).

findings.title: Most relative article URLs are not converted to source URLs
findings.body: The conversion only handles `href`/`src` values beginning with `/`. Ordinary relative references such as `images/photo.jpg`, `../next-page`, and fragment links remain relative to the Discourse topic/embed URL rather than the imported article, so common images and links break. Protocol-relative URLs are also incorrectly rewritten as paths on the source host. Resolve URLs with the article URL as the base (for example via `URI.join`) instead of concatenating only root-relative paths.

findings.title: The Disqus import command silently drops its established category option
findings.body: The command no longer declares `--category`/`-c`, and the replacement `TopicEmbed.import_remote` call has no way to pass a category. Existing import automation using that documented Thor option now fails with an unknown switch, while invocations without it can no longer import threads into the requested category and instead use the default. Preserve the option and pass the resolved category through the embed-import creation path, or explicitly provide a compatible migration path.
